issues.description: The solution for Aufgabe 01 uses an alias for the id column (id AS Kennung) while the problem statement explicitly instructs students not to rename columns with AS unless requested. This creates a structural mismatch between the instructional constraint and the provided reference solution and may confuse students about whether column renaming is permitted or required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution and template consistent with the instruction: remove the alias in the reference solution (use SELECT id, name, art, url ...) or, alternatively, update the problem statement to explicitly allow/require renaming with AS for Aufgabe 01. Ensure templates and solutions follow the same convention so students are not confused.

issues.description: The problem asks students to output the ID, Name, Art and URL of Freibäder (explicitly requesting those column names and warning not to rename columns with AS). The solution, however, renames the ID column to 'Kennung' via an alias (id AS Kennung). This introduces an inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the municipality/swimming-pool ID) across artifacts and contradicts the instruction not to rename columns, creating unnecessary mapping confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Do not alias the id column; select it as 'id' (or 'ID' if capitalization is required by convention) to match the problem statement. For example: SELECT id, name, art, url FROM Schwimmbad WHERE art='Freibad'; (or adjust the problem text to explicitly accept the alias 'Kennung' if that was intentional).
